about: Lesson F3, gradients. Computed by tools/school/fill_gradients.mjs from system/school/gradients.mjs and the attention lab's model.json. Do not edit by hand.

bowl.about: f(v) = 1/2 (v - c)^T H (v - c), axes turned 30 degrees. Curvatures from a finite-difference Hessian at the minimum. predictedBound = 2 / largest curvature; measuredBound = largest step whose runs shrink, found by bisection on real runs. Runs: 60 steps from (-2, 2) at multiples of the predicted bound; perStepFactor is the measured shrink (<1) or growth (>1) per step of the distance to the minimum.

rosenbrock.about: f = (1 - x)^2 + 100 (y - x^2)^2 from (-1.2, 1), fixed step 0.001, 20000 steps; path thinned to 200 points. Curvatures from a finite-difference Hessian. The stable step at the minimum is 2 / largest curvature there.

twoValleys.about: f = (x^2 - 1)^2 + 1.5 (y - 0.4 x)^2 + 0.2 x. Step 0.05 until |grad| < 1e-9. basin[j][i] is -1 when descent from that grid point ends in the left valley, +1 for the right; grid spans [-2, 2]^2, rows are y.

gradientCheck.about: Worst relative error |exact - numeric| / (|exact| + |numeric|) of each surface's gradient against central differences (h = 1e-5) at four points; the controls flip the gradient's sign or swap its two components and must fail.

landscape.about: Held-out loss (first 64 rows of the corpus's held-out set) on a 21 x 21 grid of theta + a d1 + b d2, a and b in [-1, 1], for the trained model and for the same model at its initialisation (seed 7). d1, d2 are seeded Gaussian directions with filter-wise normalisation (Li et al. 2018); values[j][i] has b = alphas[j], a = alphas[i]. slopeBackward is grad . d from the backward pass; slopeFiniteDiff is the same slope by central differences (h = 0.01).
landscape.note: A 2D slice shows the loss on one flat sheet through a space with thousands of dimensions. It can show whether the trained point sits in a basin along these two directions, how wide that basin is relative to the weights' own size, and how the trained point differs from the starting point. It cannot show the loss along any other direction, so a slice that looks like a bowl does not prove the point is a minimum, and a smooth slice does not rule out sharp directions elsewhere. Two random directions in high dimension are nearly at right angles to each other and to the gradient, so the slice usually misses the steepest way down.

gradientNorm.about: Global L2 norm of the gradient of the mean held-out loss over all parameters, from the model's own backward pass (lossAndGrad), on 64 and 256 held-out rows. Training clips the gradient at norm 1.0.

oneNumber.about: Every weight fixed except s, which multiplies the readout matrix wout (s = 1 is the trained model). dL/ds comes from the real backward pass by the chain rule. sStar is where dL/ds = 0 (bisection); curvature is d2L/ds2 by central differences of dL/ds. Descents start at s = 0.05 with 40 steps each; the control follows +dL/ds and climbs.
